business_patterns.top_pattern: GA authorized acute hospital spend is concentrated in three providers
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL / authorized inpatient care
key_driver_codes: Other Disorders of Nervous System with CC
Other Circulatory System Diagnoses with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: In GA, authorized PPO Local acute hospital spend is rising because volume is concentrated in a small set of hospitals, with added unit-cost pressure at two of them. MEMORIAL HEALTH UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER and NORTHSIDE HOSPITAL CHEROKEE show both more admissions and higher paid per admit, while PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER is mainly a volume story despite lower paid per admit. This is a provider concentration issue first, not a broad market-wide increase.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A few contracted hospitals are driving most of the increase, so targeted UM and reimbursement action can address a large share of the spend.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM, reimbursement, and network review on these three hospitals to test medical necessity, level-of-care management, and contract performance for the main nervous system, circulatory, liver, and musculoskeletal inpatient cases.
evidence_summary: MEMORIAL HEALTH UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER added about +$2.4M with 114 more admissions and about +$2.3K paid per admit.
NORTHSIDE HOSPITAL CHEROKEE added about +$1.8M with 110 more admissions and about +$1.3K paid per admit.
PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER added about +$2.3M with 172 more admissions, even though paid per admit fell by about $2.2K.
Key inpatient drivers include Other Disorders of Nervous System with CC and Other Circulatory System Diagnoses with CC.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA authorized acute hospital growth is mostly a UCI Medical Center admission surge
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL / authorized inpatient care
key_driver_codes: Other Circulatory System Diagnoses with CC
Disorders of Liver Except Malignancy, Cirrhosis, or Alcoholic Hepatitis with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: In CA, the largest authorized acute hospital increase is concentrated at UCI MEDICAL CENTER and is primarily driven by more inpatient volume, not higher unit cost. Admissions rose materially while paid per admit declined, indicating utilization control is the main lever. Circulatory and liver-related admissions are the clearest service lines behind the increase.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is a clean utilization problem, so admission management and avoidable inpatient use should take priority over rate action.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Ask UM operations to review admission pathways and inpatient criteria at UCI MEDICAL CENTER for the main circulatory and liver case types, and quantify avoidable admits versus appropriate growth.
evidence_summary: UCI MEDICAL CENTER drove about +$1.9M of the increase with 95 more admissions.
Paid per admit at UCI MEDICAL CENTER fell by about $3.1K, confirming the increase is mainly volume-led.
Other Circulatory System Diagnoses with CC and liver-related admissions added about +$0.2M combined.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NY authorized acute hospital pressure is concentrated at NYU Langone Hospital Long Island
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NY / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL / authorized inpatient care
business_patterns.pattern_details: In NY, authorized PPO Local acute hospital spend is concentrated almost entirely at NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND. Both admissions and paid per admit increased, making this a combined utilization and reimbursement pressure point rather than a pure volume change. The concentration at one provider makes the issue highly actionable.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single hospital is driving a material increase, so targeted contract and utilization work can move results quickly.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Escalate NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND for focused network and UM review, including admission appropriateness, case management, and reimbursement performance on the growing inpatient cases.
evidence_summary: NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND added about +$1.3M.
Admissions increased by 47 while paid per admit increased by about $2.8K.
The signal is concentrated enough to support provider-specific action rather than a broad NY response.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorization coding and facility mapping issues must be cleared before business action
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / OH / GA / authorization coding and facility classification
key_driver_codes: Other Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue Diagnoses with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Part of the observed increase is tied to authorization code movement and unmapped facility classification rather than a confirmed care-delivery change. CA and OH show material authorization distribution shifts, and GA and CA also show spend assigned to a 'Not Mapped' facility bucket. These signals should be validated before any utilization, reimbursement, or network intervention is launched.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If the increase is partly a coding or mapping artifact, teams could chase the wrong providers or services and miss the real business issue.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send these segments to data quality and UM operations to reconcile authorization coding, confirm facility mapping, and reclassify 'Not Mapped' claims before downstream policy or provider action.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The source groups explicitly flag authorization or mapping shifts and require validation before action.
evidence_summary: CA shows about +$0.9M tied to AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION with Ungroupable claims.
OH shows about +$0.5M tied to AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION, concentrated in musculoskeletal inpatient claims.
GA has about +$0.1M in a 'Not Mapped' facility bucket, and CA has another +$47K in the same bucket.
These findings are flagged as validation issues rather than confirmed operational change.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorized non-acute settings are adding spend across SNF, critical access, and rehab
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA / CA / OH / PA / NH / PPO Local / SNF - FREE STANDING, CRITICAL ACCESS, and Physical Rehab
key_driver_codes: Other Disorders of Nervous System with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Outside acute hospitals, authorized PPO Local spend is also rising in SNF, critical access, and rehab settings. Some of this is clearly volume-led, especially in GA SNF and GA critical access, while CA SNF, PA SNF, and rehab settings add a unit-cost component. The business lever is site-of-care management across post-acute and lower-acuity facilities, not just acute inpatient controls.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If discharge routing, authorization criteria, or post-acute contracting are loose, spend can continue to migrate into non-acute settings even after acute hospital actions are taken.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Have UM and network teams jointly review discharge pathways, admission criteria, and contracted rates for SNF, critical access, and rehab settings in these segments, starting with GA and CA.
evidence_summary: CA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.5M, including about 12 more admissions and roughly +$1.5K paid per admit.
GA CRITICAL ACCESS added about +$0.3M from 11 more admissions, while GA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.3M from 20 more admissions.
PA and OH SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.2M combined with higher paid per admit in both settings.
NH Physical Rehab added about +$91K from 2 admissions at about $45.5K paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic inpatient Med/Surg cases emerged in CA and NY
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / NY / IP Med/Surg / rare high-cost inpatient cases
key_driver_codes: Heart Transplant or Implant of Heart Assist System with MCC
Spinal Fusion Except Cervical with Spinal Curvature, Malignancy, Infection or Extensive Fusions with CC
AC CHRN COMB SYSTOLIC & DIASTOL CHF
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA and NY show a small number of very high-cost inpatient Med/Surg cases that materially lifted spend. The largest examples are a heart transplant or heart assist case at UCI MEDICAL CENTER and a spinal fusion case at NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND. This is not a broad utilization trend; it is a rare-case outlier pattern that needs case-level review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can materially move results and require different action than broad population management.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send these cases to the clinical agent for case-level severity and appropriateness review, and confirm reimbursement terms for transplant and complex spine services.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is driven by very small numbers of high-cost cases flagged as low-baseline and small-volume outliers.
evidence_summary: UCI MEDICAL CENTER had 1 heart transplant or heart assist case adding about +$288K.
NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND had 1 complex spinal fusion case adding about +$196K.
The remaining liver-related cases are much smaller and do not change the outlier-driven story.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Atrial fibrillation ablation with left atrial appendage closure is an emerging high-cost inpatient pattern
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA / NY / IP Med/Surg / Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Closure and Cardiac Ablation
key_driver_codes: Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Closure and Cardiac Ablation
business_patterns.pattern_details: A specific inpatient cardiac procedure is emerging in both GA and NY and is material despite low case counts. Memorial Health University Medical Center and NYU Langone Hospital Long Island together account for the entire pattern, with high paid per admit on atrial fibrillation cases. Because the procedure is recurring across two providers, it warrants focused clinical and payment review rather than broad inpatient action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is a narrow but costly procedural pattern with a clear opportunity for targeted medical policy, UM, and reimbursement review.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route these cases for clinical policy review on inpatient appropriateness and to reimbursement teams to confirm payment terms for this combined cardiac procedure.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is based on a small number of admissions with high paid per admit and low-baseline flags.
evidence_summary: MEMORIAL HEALTH UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER added about +$295K from 6 admissions at roughly $49.2K paid per admit.
NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND added about +$221K from 3 admissions at roughly $73.7K paid per admit.
All of the increase is tied to Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Closure and Cardiac Ablation on atrial fibrillation diagnoses.

business_patterns.top_pattern: GA clinical spend is concentrated in a narrow set of inpatient sepsis, circulatory, and neurologic cases
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA / IP Med/Surg and NF / concentrated diagnosis mix
key_driver_codes: Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with MCC
Other Disorders of Nervous System with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: GA clinical growth is not broad-based; it is concentrated in a narrow set of inpatient and nursing-facility diagnoses. The largest volume-led signal is sepsis and related circulatory admissions at PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, while additional spend comes from neurologic, myopathy, myocarditis, and pericarditis cases in IP Med/Surg and NF. This mix suggests targeted clinical pathway and coding review is more appropriate than broad program changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Focused diagnosis clusters can often be managed through targeted clinical pathways, documentation review, and site-of-care management rather than system-wide interventions.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send the GA diagnosis clusters to the clinical agent and UM operations for targeted review of sepsis admission drivers, neurologic rehabilitation pathways, and coding consistency on the emerging myocarditis, pericarditis, and myopathy cases.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Part of the pattern comes from low-baseline emerging diagnoses, so case identification and coding should be confirmed before broad action.
evidence_summary: PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER added about +$243K from 18 more sepsis-related admissions.
NF cases for Other Abnormalities Gait & Mobility and Unspecified Cord Compression added about +$145K and +$103K.
IP Med/Surg Critical Illness Myopathy added about +$132K across 5 admissions.
Additional rare IP Med/Surg myocarditis and pericarditis cases added about +$117K combined.

executive_summary.headline: Most of the increase is concentrated in authorized PPO Local hospital spend in GA, CA, and NY, with a second tier of non-acute site-of-care pressure and several validation and rare-case clinical issues.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: The clearest business story is provider concentration: a small set of acute hospitals accounts for most of the added spend, with GA showing the largest combined volume and unit-cost pressure and CA showing a mostly utilization-led surge at UCI MEDICAL CENTER. Before acting broadly, CA, OH, and parts of GA need authorization and facility-mapping validation, while non-acute settings and a few rare high-cost inpatient case types should be handled through targeted UM, network, reimbursement, and clinical reviews.
recommended_focus_order: GA acute hospital provider concentration under authorization
Authorization coding and facility mapping validation in CA, OH, and GA
CA and NY acute/provider actions plus non-acute site-of-care controls

notes: Focus was kept on the highest-impact authorization, provider concentration, site-of-care, validation, and clinically actionable outlier themes.
